target: contact hardening gap and assumption audit after production deploy

findings.description: Production deployment ca9d838f-6723-455f-ad35-2e634fbf26a9 was uploaded from a dirty worktree while HEAD still points at origin/main commit ab45782, so a normal Git-backed rebuild can overwrite the live fix.

The body size cap only uses Content-Length. Multipart requests created without a Content-Length are parsed by request.formData() before any byte cap is enforced, so large chunked/unknown-length bodies can still consume runtime memory/CPU.

Live smoke verified missing-token fail-closed behavior and confirmed TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY exists, but did not prove the legacy PUBLIC_WEB3FORMS_KEY value is present/valid or that a solved Turnstile token results in a delivered Web3Forms submission.

Default Turnstile hostname validation allows taranity.com and www.taranity.com only. The Cloudflare deployment URL was shared as a verification URL, but a token solved on ca9d838f.taranity.pages.dev would be rejected unless the Turnstile widget/domain config and TURNSTILE_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES include that host.

The browser suite verifies static Turnstile markup and the missing-token gate, but it does not prove the Turnstile iframe renders successfully, a token is produced, or a real positive contact submission succeeds.
The temporary PUBLIC_WEB3FORMS_KEY fallback keeps production working, but it preserves a confusing secret name and should be removed after Cloudflare receives WEB3FORMS_ACCESS_KEY.
If the Turnstile script is blocked or fails to render, the form asks the visitor to complete the verification above even when no usable challenge is visible.
form.dataset.bound is set before required child elements are validated, so a malformed or partially swapped form would be marked bound and skipped on a later retry.
